cat_collaboration.note: Claude labels barrier origin/actors (manager, peers, teammates, clients, suppliers) as Collaboration/Inclusion. NotebookLM gives no collaboration metric, only barriers BA06 (lack of collaboration between business partners) and BA10 (non-inclusive communication) as factors.

cat_devex.note: Greiler, Storey and Noda (2022) actionable DX framework adapted as structure and interview guide, but no feedback loops / cognitive load / flow dimensions; Claude says it is not used as a measurement instrument.

cat_survey.note: Self-rated VAS pain scale within interviews about perceptions of barriers.

evidence.quote: we conducted a field study, following the qualitative research principles outlined by Singer et al. (2008) and Stol and Fitzgerald (2018). This method allowed us to examine the phenomenon in a real-world setting through semi-structured interviews with 21 women working in keystone organizations.
The interview guide included unguided and guided impressions stage questions, and the responses were analyzed using thematic coding inspired by the initial steps of Grounded Theory
Using the findings from that MLR as input, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 21 women who are part of different development teams within organizations classified as keystone organizations

Our respondents came from different sectors of the industry, with 16 out of the 21 operating in the financial market, three in the insurance market, three in the oil and gas market, and two in the services market.

Thus, in the second part of the interview, the interviewee was asked to evaluate the barrier, on a scale of 0 to 10, how much pain each barrier represents for her, with 0: no pain and 10: unbearable pain.
Lesage and Berjot (2011) performed a study in which VAS scale was used to occupational stress assessment.
